accepted.question: Describe six techniques by which malware infects a host or propagates itself, and the effect of each technique.

marking_points.point: A boot sector infector saves the original master boot record elsewhere before overwriting it with an infected version, so the system then boots using the infected MBR.
marking_points.quote: Save the original MBR in a safe location
marking_points.entailment_reason: The quote confirms saving the original MBR but does not state that it is overwritten with an infected version or that the system boots from the infected MBR.

marking_points.point: A COM-file infector appends the virus body to the program and replaces the program's entry point with a jump into the virus body.
marking_points.quote: Replace a program entry point with a jump to a virus body

marking_points.point: A COM-file infector restores the original entry point and transfers control back to it once the virus code has finished executing.
marking_points.quote: Virus code restores the original entry point and jumps to it after its own execution
marking_points.entailment_reason: The quote directly states that virus code restores the original entry point and jumps to it after execution, matching the marking point.

marking_points.point: An EXE-file infector overwrites the program header so that the entry point is switched to the virus.
marking_points.quote: Over write a program header to switch the entry point to a virus

marking_points.point: An EXE-file infector lets the infected program jump to its original entry point during execution, so the host still appears to run normally.
marking_points.quote: Jump to the original entry point during execution
marking_points.entailment_reason: The quote confirms jumping to the original entry point during execution but does not mention EXE-file infectors or that the host appears to run normally.

marking_points.point: A rootkit is typically installed after a vulnerability has been found and detected, so that the infected computer stays under the malware author's control.
marking_points.quote: They are usually installed after a vulnerability has been found and detected so that the infected computer continues to be under the control of the malware author.

questions.question: Refer to your answer in (a). Explain six ways Windows security mechanisms manage users, objects and access, and why their complexity can itself become a security risk.

marking_points.point: Windows offers elaborate built-in mechanisms covering user accounts, objects and access control.
marking_points.quote: Windows systems contain complex security mechanisms for user account and object management as well as access control.

marking_points.point: Discretionary access control lists allow detailed control over diverse objects both in the OS and in applications.
marking_points.quote: DACS enable ﬁne-grained access control of heterogeneous entities in Windows itself as well as applications.

marking_points.point: Because the mechanisms are so complex, poor configuration or coding flaws can cause serious security breaches.
marking_points.quote: The complexity of Windows security mechanisms is also its enemy: misconﬁguration as well as implementation bugs may lead to severe security incidents.

marking_points.point: Active Directory, introduced with Windows 2000, is a directory service that organises users, groups, credentials, resources and policies.
marking_points.quote: Active directory introduced in Windows 2000 is an LDAP-like directory service for organization of system resources:

marking_points.point: Security attributes for a running subject are held in a token that maps the principal to the subject and is passed on to child processes.
marking_points.quote: Security credentials for a subject are stored in a token.

marking_points.point: The registry stores security-relevant hives such as the SAM database, security logs and program paths.
marking_points.quote: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE	\ SAM: SAM database

questions.question: Explain how the Samy worm used cross-site scripting to infect MySpace user profiles, and what made the attack so widespread.

marking_points.point: The worm injected JavaScript into a user profile by writing to document.body.innerHTML.
marking_points.quote: Inject Javascript into a user proﬁle using document.body.innerHTML

marking_points.point: It retrieved the list of the user's heroes by issuing a GET request to a user profile.
marking_points.quote: Get the list of user’s heros by using a GET on a user proﬁle

marking_points.point: It added Samy as a friend by performing an XML-HTTP request against the addFriends page.
marking_points.quote: Add Samy as a ﬁeld by performing XML-HTTP on the addFriends page

marking_points.point: Any visitor to an infected profile had their own profile and friends list infected, enabling self-propagation.
marking_points.quote: Any user who visits an infected user’s page will gets proﬁle infected with Javascript and his friends list infected with Samy

marking_points.point: The worm reached a very large scale, infecting roughly one million MySpace profiles.
marking_points.quote: Eventually about 1,000,000 MySpace proﬁles were infected.

marking_points.point: The underlying weakness is that any web application returning user input without filtering is a potential XSS vulnerability.
marking_points.quote: Any web application that returns user input without ﬁltering is a potential XSS vulnerability!

questions.question: Explain how a substitution cipher works and what serves as its key.

marking_points.point: Encryption replaces each plaintext letter with a different letter to produce the ciphertext.
marking_points.quote: In substitution ciphers, we replace the plain-text letters with other letters

marking_points.point: The substitution rule itself functions as the key of the cipher.
marking_points.quote: The substitution rule is the key

questions.question: Describe six (6) points about the access control matrix, access control list and capability structures, covering how each is organised and its stated advantages or disadvantages.

marking_points.point: The access control matrix is presented as a basic control structure.
marking_points.quote: ACM is a basic control structure.

marking_points.point: The ACM is credited with clarity of definition and being easy to verify.
marking_points.quote:
Advantages:
clarity of deﬁnition
easy to verify

marking_points.point: The ACM suffers from poor scalability and poor handling of changes.
marking_points.quote:
Disadvantages:
poor scalability
poor handling of changes

marking_points.point: An ACL is an object-centred description of access rights, illustrated by entries such as bill.doc granting Bob read and write.
marking_points.quote:
ACL is an object-centered description of access rights:
bill.doc:	{Bob:	read, write}

marking_points.point: ACL advantages include easy access to object access rights and relatively easy management using abstractions.
marking_points.quote:
Advantages:
easy access to object access rights
relative easiness of management using abstractions

marking_points.point: ACL disadvantages include poor overview of access rights per subject, difficulty of revocation and difficulty of sharing.
marking_points.quote:
Disadvantages:
poor overview of access rights per subject
difﬁculty of revocation
difﬁculty of sharing

questions.question: List TWO (2) goals of access control and state what a reference monitor does.

marking_points.point: One goal of access control is granting access.
marking_points.quote:
Goals of access control:
Granting access

marking_points.point: A reference monitor is responsible for making authorization decisions.
marking_points.quote: Reference monitor makes authorization decisions.

questions.question: Describe six techniques by which malware infects a host or propagates itself, and the effect of each technique.

marking_points.point: A boot sector infector saves the original master boot record elsewhere before overwriting it with an infected version, so the system then boots using the infected MBR.
marking_points.quote: Save the original MBR in a safe location

marking_points.point: A COM-file infector appends the virus body to the program and replaces the program's entry point with a jump into the virus body.
marking_points.quote: Replace a program entry point                                   with a jump to a virus body

marking_points.point: A COM-file infector restores the original entry point and transfers control back to it once the virus code has finished executing.
marking_points.quote: Virus code restores the original                                 entry point and jumps to it after                                     its own execution

marking_points.point: An EXE-file infector overwrites the program header so that the entry point is switched to the virus.
marking_points.quote: Over write a program header to switch the entry point to a virus

marking_points.point: An EXE-file infector lets the infected program jump to its original entry point during execution, so the host still appears to run normally.
marking_points.quote: Jump to the original entry point                               during execution

marking_points.point: A rootkit is typically installed after a vulnerability has been found and detected, so that the infected computer stays under the malware author's control.
marking_points.quote: They are usually installed after a vulnerability has been found and detected so that the infected computer continues to be under the control of the malware author.

questions.question: State six facts about biometric mechanisms and technologies as presented in the course, covering the definition, the categories, and specific biometric technologies.

marking_points.point: A biometric is defined as a physiological or behavioural characteristic of a human being that can distinguish one person from another and can theoretically be used for identification or verification of identity.
marking_points.quote: A biometric is a physiological or behavioural characteristic of a human being that can distinguish one person from another and that theoretically can be used for identification or verification of identity.

marking_points.point: Biometric applications available today are divided into two sectors: psychological and behavioural.
marking_points.quote: Biometric applications available today are categorized into 2 sectors

marking_points.point: The psychological sector includes iris, fingerprints, hand, retinal and face recognition.
marking_points.quote: Psychological: Iris, Fingerprints, Hand, Retinal and Face recognition

marking_points.point: The behavioural sector includes voice, typing pattern and signature.
marking_points.quote: Behavioural: Voice, Typing pattern, Signature

marking_points.point: Fingerprint processing divides the print into loops, whorls and arch and calculates minutiae points (ridge endings).
marking_points.quote: Divides print into loops, whorls and arch

marking_points.point: Iris scanning scans the unique pattern of the iris, which is coloured and visible from far, and requires no touch, thereby overcoming retinal scanner issues.
marking_points.quote: Scans unique pattern of iris

questions.question: State six preventive network security mechanisms and, for each, one function it performs in protecting an organization's network.

marking_points.point: Firewall: it controls incoming and outgoing network traffic according to predetermined security policies.
marking_points.quote: Control incoming and outgoing traffic on network with predetermined security policies.

marking_points.point: Proxy server: it improves data security and network performance by acting as a firewall and web filter, sharing connections and caching data.
marking_points.quote: Proxy servers act as a firewall and web filter, provide shared network connections, and cache data to speed up common requests.

marking_points.point: Network segmentation: it creates boundaries between network segments whose computing assets share a common function, risk or role.
marking_points.quote: Boundaries between network segments where computing assets within the segment have a common function, risk or role within an organization.

marking_points.point: Remote access VPN: it gives individual hosts or clients remote and secure access to the organization's network.
marking_points.quote: Provides remote and secure access to an organization network to individual hosts or clients

marking_points.point: Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA): a user is granted only the access and permission required to fulfil the role.
marking_points.quote: A user should only has access and permission that required to fulfill the role

marking_points.point: Intrusion Detection/Prevention Systems (IDS/IPS): they detect or prevent attacks such as brute force, Denial-of-Service and exploits of network vulnerabilities.
marking_points.quote: To detect or prevent the network security attacks such as brute force attacks, Denial-of-Service attacks and exploits of network vulnerabilities.

questions.question: Discuss three design criteria of Kerberos and three motivations for adopting single sign-on in distributed environments.

marking_points.point: Kerberos must prevent eavesdropping by ensuring that passwords are never transmitted in clear text.
marking_points.quote: Security against eavesdropping: no                                       password transmission in clear text.

marking_points.point: Kerberos must guarantee reliability by requiring prior authentication for every use of a service.
marking_points.quote: Reliability: every use of a service requires                            prior authentication.

marking_points.point: Kerberos must be transparent so that the user is unaware of any authentication beyond the initial login.
marking_points.quote: Transparency: user is not aware of any                            authentication beyond an initial login.

marking_points.point: Kerberos must be scalable to support a large number of servers and clients.
marking_points.quote: Scalability: support for a large number of                                          servers and clients.

marking_points.point: Single sign-on reduces the burden on users to memorize passwords.
marking_points.quote: Reduce the need to memorize passwords

marking_points.point: Single sign-on reduces the time users spend typing passwords.
marking_points.quote: Reduce the time spent on typing passwords

questions.question: Explain six components and functions of the NGSCB architecture, focusing on the Nexus and the Nexus Computing Agent.

marking_points.point: The Nexus is a security kernel that is authenticated during boot.
marking_points.quote: Security kernel, authenticated on boot

marking_points.point: The Nexus provides an application interface to the TPM.
marking_points.quote: Application interface to TPM

marking_points.point: The Nexus Computing Agent is a trusted software component.
marking_points.quote: Trusted software component

marking_points.point: The NCA runs in a trusted mode that communicates with the Nexus.
marking_points.quote: Runs in trusted mode that communicates with Nexus

marking_points.point: The Nexus is a special kernel forming the core of the trusted operating environment.
marking_points.quote: Special kernel (core of the trusted operating)

marking_points.point: The Nexus isolates normal-mode processes from trusted-mode processes differently in memory.
marking_points.quote: Isolate the process of  normal mode and                                                  trusted mode                                                                                differently in memory

questions.question: Explain the distinction between a vulnerability, a threat and an attack, and describe how organisations counter threats arising from forces of nature and from malicious web input.

marking_points.point: A vulnerability is a weakness in a system that can be exploited to damage its assets.
marking_points.quote: Vulnerabilities: Weakness of a system that can be exploited to damage assets

marking_points.point: A threat is only a potential violation of security, not yet an actual one.
marking_points.quote: Threats: A threat is a                                                          “potential” violation of                                                                    security

marking_points.point: An attack is the actual violation of security that has occurred.
marking_points.quote: Attacks: The actual                                                                               violation of security

marking_points.point: Forces of nature are counted among the most dangerous threats to information systems.
marking_points.quote: Forces of nature are among the most dangerous threats

marking_points.point: Organisations must put controls in place to limit the damage from such threats and prepare contingency plans so operations can continue.
marking_points.quote: Organizations must implement controls to limit damage and prepare contingency plans for continued operations
